scope_depth.judgment: Strong fit and substantive depth; within 1,300-1,800 words and the seven-URL ceiling.
scope_depth.evidence: At 1,784 words and five primary URLs, it compares one-step spatial tiling, one-step plane/window reuse, and multi-step overlap or time-skew. It gives explicit halo/work and storage arithmetic, physical-boundary and tail limitations, one measured loss case and one architecture-dependent win case, and a bounded selection rule.

novelty_and_redundancy.judgment: Material focused increment, with adjacent but nonduplicative background.
novelty_and_redundancy.new_increment: The center is reuse across successive time levels and the crossover among halo recomputation, plane reuse, capacity, boundary policy, and repeated-use count.
novelty_and_redundancy.prior_scope_comparison: R763 is a broad pipeline/residency and stencil survey; R773 concerns model-prefill chunk/tile/tail geometry; R832 concerns in-kernel roles, prefetch distance, barriers, and stage ownership. R835's temporal reuse and halo-cost model remain distinct when kept at this focus.

primary_source_verification.status: Material claims were checked against the cited primary documentation and papers. The CiteseerX PDF endpoint did not render as a normal page; its indexed text from the primary PDF exposed the relevant claims, so that source check has a retrieval limitation.

confirmed.claims: Intel's dated ISO3DFD walkthrough describes the 16th-order radius-eight stencil, 9-value front plus 8-value back window, one new Z value per sweep step, XY local_accessor staging, one SYCL kernel per time level, the exact local tile extent form, and its Gen9/Gen12LP performance caution. The page marks its sample MIT licensed.
confirmed.limit: The article is a mutable webpage; no linked sample commit was pinned. It is documentation evidence, not a performance result for other devices.

confirmed.claims: SYCL 2020 revision 12 specifies local_accessor storage per work-group and group_barrier coordination among work-items in that group.
confirmed.limit: The specification does not promise a local-memory capacity, implementation speed, or hardware mapping; group_barrier does not provide a grid-wide barrier.

confirmed.claims: The indexed primary paper text confirms the radius-one 3-D seven-point diffusion workload, its own-value boundary rule, Fermi's L1 reuse and negative explicit-staging result, and Kepler results including 287 GFLOP/s and 1.23x over SHM-WARP for TEMP.
confirmed.limit: Direct PDF page rendering failed; keep claims attributed to the paper's Fermi/Kepler hardware and its stated boundary rule.

confirmed.claims: AN5D version 4 reports first-order Tesla V100 temporal-blocking depths of roughly 8-15 for 2-D and 3-5 for 3-D, with high-order 3-D box counterexamples from register pressure and halo ratio.
confirmed.limit: These are tuned CUDA/V100 results, not general defaults.

confirmed.claims: EBISU version 1 reports A100 3-D seven-point rates of 151 versus 197 GCells/s for SM-overlap versus device tiling. It also reports that LST can consume on-chip space and reduce blocking depth; removing LST changed nominal throughput from 2.7 to 2.9 TB/s while useful throughput fell from 2.4 to 2.3 TB/s.
confirmed.limit: The report preserves these as one CUDA/A100 counterexample, not a transferable SYCL or BMG measurement.

primary_source_verification.arithmetic: The B=32,T=4 2-D and B=16,T=4/8 3-D update, footprint, byte, and boundary-share examples recompute from the displayed formulas. They are idealized box-halo counts, not measured traffic, occupancy, or exact star-stencil work.

applicability_and_evidence_limits.main_result: No Strata implementation, local performance, Xe2/BMG behavior, or adoption claim is established.
applicability_and_evidence_limits.limits: The report correctly separates within-step plane/window reuse from across-step temporal reuse and labels rectangular halo arithmetic as a screening model. Physical-boundary percentages apply to the stated non-periodic boundary interpretation; actual boundary injection and stencil shape remain workload-specific.

main_retrieval.retrieve_when: A concrete general GPU/ASIC stencil question needs a comparison of temporal depth, halo recomputation, plane reuse, or boundary cost.

reusable_index_topics: Across-time halo expansion versus a one-step sliding-plane/register window.
Local capacity, tile count, physical boundaries, and short temporal tails as time-depth crossover terms.
Cache hierarchy and useful-work accounting can reverse apparent temporal-blocking wins.
R835.outcome: Retain as knowledge archive. Main should not read the collection body on arrival.

scope_depth.judgment: Strong and source-specific; within 1,200-1,800 words and the eight-URL ceiling.
scope_depth.evidence: At 1,553 words and five primary URLs, it traces actual local typed/FP32 boundaries, sizes the three large GDN intermediates, compares a vLLM prefill wrapper contract with an FLA recurrent kernel, and gives numerical, state, ordering, projection, and full-path gates.

novelty_and_redundancy.judgment: Useful source-specific increment over overlapping precision and state surveys.
novelty_and_redundancy.new_increment: It maps the actual integrated native16 GDN call path and names QKV, Z, hbuf, redundant y, gate scalars, convolution history, and recurrent state with per-token byte counts. It asks whether direct typed producer outputs and typed consumers can be added while retaining FP32 local recurrence and persistent state.
novelty_and_redundancy.prior_scope_comparison: R782 covers framework activation and persistent-state contracts; R820 covers state materialization versus rematerialization; R822 covers general non-GEMM low-precision kernels; R828/R829 cover lossy and lossless transport. R836's local-source path and precise GDN convolution/recurrence seam are incremental, not a duplicate generic dtype survey.

local_source_cross_check.status: The listed live source files confirm the report's main call graph and tensor types.
confirmed: Native16 mix writes BF16 m.mixed_bf and FP16 m.mixed_h; native_proj writes FP32 QKV and Z; FP32 AB feeds FP32 gate/beta transforms.
Float-pointer GDN convolution and recurrence consume/produce FP32 block tensors; the recurrence also writes an FP16 output. The native16 branch consumes that FP16 output for the output projection.
The recurrence state is FP32 with physical (S, H_v, S) storage and h modulo h_k head pairing; convolution history is separate FP32 storage.
The computed GDN reservation demand is 144,128 bytes/token. At T=8192 its arithmetic sum is 1126 MiB, but the actual shared arena extent is max(GDN, QSA, MoE) demand, not the sum of all three.
local_source_cross_check.limits: Source tracing and hashes are local-file evidence, not a Git revision assertion or performance profile. The assignment-supplied 6354f0b4 identifier was not independently checked.

primary_source_verification.status: Immutable vLLM and FLA commits and their root licenses were checked; the FLA chunk-size contract was checked at the same pinned commit.

confirmed.claims: The pinned fi_chunk_gated_delta_rule wrapper optionally normalizes Q/K, preserves Q/K/V input tensor dtypes at the call boundary, converts initial state, gate, and beta to FP32, passes exp(g), and returns the FlashInfer result.
confirmed.limit: This proves wrapper arguments only; it does not inspect FlashInfer's internals for hidden conversion, prove output-state layout, show SYCL support, or establish BMG support.

confirmed.claims: The pinned vLLM root license is Apache-2.0.

The pinned Triton recurrence loads Q/K/V, gate and beta to FP32 local values, loads the initial carry into FP32 local state, applies decay and beta-scaled update, stores output in its output tensor type, and stores final state through the final-state tensor's type.
confirmed.limit: This is a Triton implementation reference; it establishes no BMG/SYCL support or equivalence to Strata's physical state layout.

confirmed.claims: The pinned chunk API documents chunk sizes 16, 32, or 64 and initial/final-state shapes.
confirmed.limit: The chunked WY decomposition is different from Strata's recurrence and needs separate state/output parity.

confirmed.claims: The pinned FLA root license is MIT.

corrections.issue: The report says FLA final state is written in the requested state-output dtype.
corrections.correction: At the pinned fused_recurrent.py revision, output_final_state allocates final_state explicitly with dtype=torch.float32. The kernel casts output to the output tensor dtype, but the final state has no requested dtype option in this wrapper and is FP32.

corrections.issue: The 1126 MiB T=8192 number could be read as the current chunk arena allocation.
corrections.correction: Label it the source-derived GDN reservation demand. The local planner allocates one shared region sized as max(GDN, QSA, MoE); it is neither a measured peak nor necessarily the selected region extent.
corrections.severity: precision correction; the report already disclaims a measured peak

numerical_and_control_flow_review.judgment: The report accurately withholds semantic equivalence and identifies the key incompatibilities.
confirmed_gates: Keep FP32 gate/beta transforms, recurrent accumulation and persistent carry separate from block storage.

Preserve Strata's convolution tap order/history commit, Q/K normalization and readout scale, beta and decay transforms, modulo head map, physical state layout, output norm/gate, chunk state, queue dependency, and 262144-context quality comparison.
Test FP16 and BF16 separately; do not assume native_proj can directly produce typed output or substitute native_proj16's IQ-dequant-to-F16 route without comparing actual weights and tensors.
numerical_and_control_flow_review.additional_limit: The report should describe vLLM as an API-boundary pattern only. The wrapper does not prove that the called FlashInfer implementation consumes these tensors without internal materialization.

next_knowledge_collection_scopes.title: Bank-aware local-memory layouts for tiled GPU and ASIC kernels
next_knowledge_collection_scopes.finite_question: For non-LLM kernels that stage multidimensional tiles in banked on-chip memory, compare row padding, XOR/swizzled addressing, and conflict-free transpose mappings. How do bank count/width, vector width, tile shape, lane mapping, and access phase change bank serialization and local-storage use, and when can padding or address arithmetic cost more than it saves? Include one measured win and one counterexample.
next_knowledge_collection_scopes.breadth_and_counterevidence: Use official GPU/SYCL vendor documentation and original GPU/ASIC papers or technical blogs. Derive bank-index examples for at least two layout strategies and compare them on a transpose or neighborhood tile. Separate published hardware results from source-level bank arithmetic. Include cases where the same mapping helps one access phase but hurts another or where padding increases resource pressure. Exclude temporal blocking/halo reuse, producer-consumer scheduling/barriers, global-memory sector/page transactions, generic GEMM tile tuning, and Strata adoption claims. Do not infer BMG/Xe2 bank geometry or support from another architecture.
next_knowledge_collection_scopes.report_budget: 1,300-1,700 words; at most 7 substantive primary sources; one strategy/geometry table; exact source URLs and applicability/evidence limits.
next_knowledge_collection_scopes.prerequisites: Public-source access only; local bottleneck measurements are not required for this durable knowledge collection.
next_knowledge_collection_scopes.prerequisite_evidence: AGENTS.md requests transferable SYCL and GPU/ASIC optimization research beyond current bottlenecks. Reviewed metadata describes R811's 2D-message descriptors/alignment, R832's pipeline roles and slot ownership, and R835's temporal stencil halo costs; none is centered on bank-index mapping and conflict-free layout transforms. R778/R779 cover sparse formats and global transaction/page-gather effects, which this scope explicitly excludes.
next_knowledge_collection_scopes.novelty_guard: Keep the investigation on bank mapping and local layout transforms. Do not recast it as another pipeline, stencil-temporal-blocking, global-memory coalescing, or GEMM survey.
